projects.summary: The project segments roads and occlusions (buildings, trees) in drone videos, using a segmentation model such as SAM, to support occlusion-aware vehicle detection.

projects.title: Alpine microbiome under pressure: Investigating the microbial community and its response to climate change.
projects.summary: Combined dry- and wet-lab project studying the microbial community of barren alpine mountain tops with seasonal snow cover at almost 3000 m, using metagenomics and proteomics. The work couples microbial community data with greenhouse gas emission monitoring at a field site in Crans-Montana, with periodic field visits and laboratory work in Sion.

projects.title: Composition and function of crysphere microbiomes
projects.summary: Bioinformatic project analysing in-house and publicly available metagenomes to determine the taxonomic composition and functions of cryosphere microbiomes and identify global genomic features. It is followed by a meta-analysis to find trends and patterns across different cryosphere environments.

projects.title: Molecular adaptation strategies of alpine snow microorganisms to warming
projects.summary: Laboratory-based project in which alpine snow microbes are isolated and characterised genomically for their metabolic potential in cold and warming adaptation. Isolates are cultivated at a range of temperatures and their RNA/proteins analysed to identify molecular changes and assess the thermal tolerance of cryospheric microorganisms. A bioinformatic component is included, and optional fieldwork is possible.

projects.title: Assessment and adaptation of building components for extended service lifetimes
projects.summary: Extends a digital method for assessing the environmental reclamation potential of building elements to support reuse and recycling. Possible directions include disassembly sequencing with interface inventories and knowledge graphs, impact analysis of material value chains, deterioration mechanisms of building envelopes, and non-destructive test protocols.

projects.title: Bio-inspired construction materials
projects.summary: Explores how biological structures and mechanisms can inspire next-generation natural materials and interfaces for sustainable construction. The student will experiment with material formulations, digital fabrication, re-assembly and characterisation to obtain materials with tailored functional properties.

projects.title: Pathway toward optimized life-cycle management of glass in the construction sector
projects.summary: Investigates glass products, framing systems, flat glass and glass wool used in buildings, reviewing current production, material selection, use and end-of-life practices. The goal is to identify circular economy and material recovery strategies and develop alternative variants, assessed with a bottom-up life-cycle assessment. The project is part of a collaboration with the Canton of Zurich.

projects.title: Reversible interfaces for sustainable construction
projects.summary: Researches reversible adhesion for multi-material building components to enable reuse, covering bi-material compatibility, joint geometry optimisation, fabrication and disassembly on demand. The student may study separation of existing composite elements or develop new connection methods.

projects.title: Engineering environmental microbiomes via selective ion transport
projects.summary: Project on engineering environmental microbial communities by controlling selective ion transport.

projects.title: Enrichment and isolation of fermenter bacteria from anaerobic digestion
projects.summary: Project on enriching and isolating fermentative bacteria from anaerobic digestion processes.

projects.title: Exploring Predictive Models and Machine Learning for Microbial Communities in Anaerobic Digesters
projects.summary: Project on using predictive models and machine learning to study microbial communities in anaerobic digesters.

projects.title: Investigating the physiology of CO2-reducing microbes for carbon-neutral, renewable chemical synthesis
projects.summary: Project on the physiology of CO2-reducing microbes with the aim of carbon-neutral, renewable chemical synthesis.

projects.title: Isolation of methane-oxidizing bacteria for greenhouse gas removal
projects.summary: Project on isolating methane-oxidizing bacteria for use in removing greenhouse gases.

projects.title: Soil-plant interactions: Influence of iron dynamics on plant physiology in saline soils
projects.summary: Studies how salinity, flooding and oxygen availability change iron chemistry in soils and how this affects iron availability and plant physiology. The student would build an artificial saline soil system with iron-containing minerals, assess iron geochemistry under different salinity and moisture levels, develop an imaging system to monitor plant growth, and model how salinity, moisture and iron mineralogy affect plant growth.
skills: Interest in plants and environmental processes

projects.title: Assessment of an existing bridge
projects.summary: Assessment of an existing bridge using frame finite element analysis, including ULS and fatigue verifications with recent simulation tools and traffic load models (SIA 269 revision), and, if necessary, a proposed intervention such as reinforcement or monitoring.

projects.title: Conceptual design of a footbridge
projects.summary: As part of a design competition, students draft a project basis, develop several footbridge variants, design the chosen variant, and produce two A1 technical drawing sheets with plan, elevations, sections, details and construction stages.

projects.title: Design of a typical steel building
projects.summary: Design of a typical industrial or office steel frame building, covering the floor system, lateral load resisting systems, connections and foundation, with conceptual design and verification of members and frame stability under wind and/or seismic loading. Deliverables include connection detailing drawings and a detailed calculation report.
skills: structural design software used in design offices

projects.title: Dynamic stability of steel structures under seismic excitations
projects.summary: Combines theoretical analysis and numerical modelling of the dynamic stability of steel frames under seismic excitation with shake-table tests of an idealised frame built from the MOLA Structural Kit, exploring torsional effects, soft-storey vulnerability and frame stability criteria.

projects.title: Nonlinear dynamic analysis of steel structures
projects.summary: Development of Python numerical models to simulate the dynamic response of steel structures under seismic loading, using fibre-based beam-columns or concentrated plasticity models, with results placed in design context.

projects.title: Nonlinear modelling and analysis of steel structures
projects.summary: Development of frame analysis models for steel structures to study their linear and nonlinear response through static or dynamic analysis procedures.

projects.title: Nonlinear static analysis of steel structures
projects.summary: Development of Python numerical models to simulate the nonlinear static (pushover) analysis of steel structures under wind and/or seismic loading, using fibre-based beam-columns or concentrated plasticity models, with results placed in design context (SIA 269/3, Eurocode 8 part 3).

projects.title: Seismic stability of base-isolated steel structures
projects.summary: Shaking table tests on typical steel structural configurations, compared with numerical simulations, to evaluate the influence of base isolation on structural response under earthquake shaking.

projects.title: Stability project using interactive tools (MOLA Kit)
projects.summary: Hands-on physical modelling with the MOLA Structural Kit to explore stability phenomena in frame structures, combining structural dynamics, structural stability and structural analysis.

projects.title: Automated selection of spectral windows for gas detection and isotopic ratio retrievals from HITRAN database
projects.summary: Develop a reproducible Python tool that uses the HITRAN spectroscopic database to simulate absorption spectra and rank the best spectral windows for detecting target gases and measuring isotopic ratios. The tool aims to support the design of optical greenhouse gas sensors.

projects.title: Permeance of N2O, NH3 and H2O through two-dimensional graphene membranes
projects.summary: Characterise the permeation coefficients of N2O, NH3 and H2O through atomically thin graphene membranes and benchmark them against existing PDMS membranes used in in-situ dissolved gas probes. The work also quantifies the effects of temperature and salinity.

projects.title: Characterizing the redox parameters dictating the reactivity of Mn(III)-oxides
projects.summary: Determine the thermodynamic and kinetic redox parameters of Mn(III)-oxides (hausmannite and manganite) using mediated electrochemical analyses, and quantify how carbonate, organic matter and ligands affect their reactivity and electron transfer.

projects.title: Effect of organic fertilizer plus additives on GHG emissions and soil properties
projects.summary: Evaluate whether organic fertilizers combined with additives, shown promising in laboratory studies, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and change soil properties under real conditions on two Swiss farms, through field GHG measurements and soil analyses.

projects.title: Field and experimental Data visualization and sharing through software application
projects.summary: Develop further a web application that imports, exports and visualises field and experimental soil and ecology data from two Swiss Alpine study sites, adding interactive maps and plots and a user interface for a broad public audience.

projects.title: Insights into organic carbon mineralization in alpine soils: A soil incubation experiment
projects.summary: Assess how soil moisture influences soil organic carbon mineralisation in Swiss alpine soils through laboratory incubation experiments, measuring respiration, redox conditions and oxygen availability and analysing the results statistically.

projects.title: Soil-plant interactions: Influence of iron dynamics on plant physiology in saline soils
projects.summary: Build an artificial saline soil system of sand and iron-bearing minerals to study how salinity and moisture change iron geochemistry and, in turn, plant growth and physiology, including developing an imaging system and a plant growth model.

projects.title: AI-Driven Prediction of River Morphology
projects.summary: Develop deep-learning models that forecast long-term planform changes of complex river systems, especially braided rivers, using satellite imagery and open-source datasets. Possible directions include new architectures and loss functions, integrating hydrologic data and evaluating model performance.

projects.title: Experiments on fluvial dunes
projects.summary: Controlled laboratory experiments in a narrow recirculating flume to study mobile sand bed dynamics under different flow conditions. High-frequency imaging of the bed and free surface will be processed to characterise bedform evolution, with an optional link to data-driven prediction of bed evolution.

projects.title: Hydrokinetic energy resource assessment methods
projects.summary: Develop an analytical or data-driven methodology to estimate the hydrokinetic energy resource available in rivers and engineered channels. The longer-term aim is an assessment of hydrokinetic potential across rural Switzerland and Europe.

projects.title: Influence of Dam Idealization on Reservoir Sedimentation Predictions in Delft3D
projects.summary: Compare alternative representations of a dam in Delft3D (such as downstream water level conditions, simplified discharge relationships and explicit hydraulic structures) to quantify how they affect simulated sediment retention and deposition. The study aims to determine the level of model complexity appropriate for different purposes.

projects.title: Morphodynamic Controls on the Evolution of Reservoir Sediment Trapping Efficiency
projects.summary: Use Delft3D to model how sediment trapping efficiency in a reservoir changes as it fills and delta deposits develop. The work will calculate trapping efficiency from sediment mass balances and relate it to storage loss, deposit distribution and flow conditions.

projects.title: Numerical tools for sediment transport and morphodynamic simulations
projects.summary: Evaluate the capability of numerical tools, mainly the BASEMENT hydro-morphodynamic software, to simulate sediment transport and bed evolution in simplified natural and laboratory configurations. Students run controlled numerical experiments to identify strengths and limitations of the tools.

projects.title: Reservoir Sedimentation at Dams: Synthesis and Expansion of Existing Datasets
projects.summary: Synthesise and expand existing datasets on reservoir sedimentation, with a focus on mitigation strategies at operational dams. The goal is a structured database linking dam characteristics, watershed properties and mitigation effectiveness, analysed for patterns. The project is in collaboration with Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

projects.title: River bedforms detection and analysis from laboratory data
projects.summary: Analyse a laboratory dataset of migrating ripples and dunes to estimate their migration speed and two-dimensional shape. The approach applies particle image velocimetry-inspired algorithms that compare consecutive image pairs.

projects.title: Sensitivity of Catchment-Scale Sediment Budget Estimates to Sediment Transport Equations and Model Parameters
projects.summary: Use the D-CASCADE sediment connectivity model on the Romanche catchment to test how sediment transport equations (Rickenmann, Wilcock-Crowe-Mueller) and input parameters such as active width, active layer depth and discharge affect sediment budget estimates. The aim is a reproducible sensitivity analysis and guidance on formula suitability and input-data priorities.

projects.title: Contemporary History Tracing: Constructing Architecture: Materials Processes Structures
projects.summary: Traces the influence of the 2005 book Constructing Architecture: Materials Processes Structures, examining where it is used as a textbook and reference, how its use differs from the authors' intention, and what its influence says about architectural practice today.

projects.title: Contractors
projects.summary: Examines the history and operating strategy of local contractors such as Orlatti and Implenia.

projects.title: Existing buildings as continued material commitments
projects.summary: Identifies buildings renovated over multiple cycles, such as exposed-concrete examples like St. Antonius Church in Basel and the Goetheanum in Dornach, to understand material expenditure as a continual commitment rather than a one-time act.

projects.title: Follow the Things: M3 Construction
projects.summary: Studies the history and planning of the M3 project in Lausanne, asking whether it is still defensible and what alternatives exist, and surveys where its construction and excavated materials come from and whether alternatives exist.

projects.title: Gabarits/Baugespanne/Building Profiles
projects.summary: Examines how building profiles (gabarits) are used, where, and why, how the practice has changed over time, and when it is helpful or misleading.

projects.title: Lausanne Main Station
projects.summary: Studies the history and planning of the new Lausanne main station, asking whether the project is still defensible and what alternatives exist.

projects.title: The City, Underground: Lausanne
projects.summary: Characterizes and precisely draws the underground of Lausanne, including parking, metro, and train infrastructure (LEB, TRIDEL), examining how these spaces were imagined, how much remains, and what the future holds for them.

projects.title: The Life of Grande Dixence as Construction Site
projects.summary: Uses the on-site journal and films of the construction process as primary material to characterize life on the construction sites of the Dixence-Cleuson hydropower complex over the decade of construction.

projects.title: Automatic georeferencing of historical cadastres
projects.summary: Develop automatic computer vision and graph neural network methods to georeference sheets of the 19th-century Napoleonic and renovated European cadastres.

projects.title: Automatic transcription of Polier notebooks
projects.summary: Automatically transcribe the handwritten Polier notebooks (1754-1791) with handwriting recognition, then use NLP-based distant reading to study environmental, social or economic history.

projects.title: Automatic vectorization of the renovated cadastre of Lausanne
projects.summary: Transform the 1888 renovated cadastre of Lausanne into vector maps using CNN-based semantic segmentation, and possibly apply handwritten text recognition to its legend.

projects.title: Beyond Cheese and Chocolate: The Economic Landscape of Historical Switzerland
projects.summary: Realign addresses from Swiss commercial registers (1883 onwards) to geographic coordinates using modern and historical place-name databases, then analyse and visualise the resulting historical economic geography of Switzerland.

projects.title: Cartonomics / Visual semiotics
projects.summary: Identify and extract the symbolic and representational visual elements of cartography using deep learning and statistical methods, to study how map conventions for relief, water, buildings and natural landscape evolved over time.

projects.title: Door-to-door
projects.summary: Conduct analyses of city directories for Lausanne over a 10-year sample, extracted through OCR, and compare trades with Paris and New York in 1880 to identify each city's economic signature.

projects.title: Enlumina
projects.summary: Index the visual elements of illustrated medieval manuscripts by segmenting depictions, annotating them against an iconographic database, and building a search engine for textual and visual similarity, with the aim of studying authorship through visual similarities.

projects.title: European Postcards
projects.summary: Geolocate historical postcards of Europe from Europeana using AI-based semantic identification and prompting, then publish the repositioned images in the Time Machine Atlas interface.

projects.title: Haussmannian transformations in Paris during the XIXth century
projects.summary: Convert the 19th-century maps of the Bibliothèque historique de la Ville de Paris into vector geometries using CNN pixelwise classification and computer vision, then quantitatively analyse the transformation of the urban fabric.

projects.title: Icono Lausanne – Reorientation of the photographic archives of the Historical Museum
projects.summary: Match the Historical Museum of Lausanne's digitised photographs to the city using photogrammetry and neural networks, estimating each shot's camera angle and position to reproject them onto 4D models.

projects.title: Lausanne 1722
projects.summary: Enrich the georeferenced and vectorised Melotte cadastre of Lausanne (1721-1722) with socio-economic information on land use, function and ownership, to serve as a historical geodata source on the city's 18th-century landscape.

projects.title: The Cultural Microscope
projects.summary: Design and build a prototype interface for exploring cultural memes, i.e. replicated visual elements tracked across tens of thousands of digitised historical maps, using embeddings and IIIF images with metadata filtering.

projects.title: The Hidden Grammar of Art History
projects.summary: Work with OCR extracted from 300,000 digitised art-object cardboards of the Replica project to realign artist-name entities and derive heuristics on the grammar of artist attribution.

projects.title: The Origins of Venice
projects.summary: Create a digital urban atlas of Venice for 1100 and 1350 from OCR-processed historiographical sources, then build an interactive cartography and analyse ownership, land use and family names.

projects.title: The space of Victorian London
projects.summary: Study how 19th and 20th century urban interventions shaped the social-spatial structure of London by enriching a dataset of building footprints and text segments from the 1890s Ordnance Survey map with infrastructure and economic data and linking it to social class information from Booth's map.

projects.title: The World as a Canvas: Multimodal Realignment of Historical Map Archives
projects.summary: Develop a multimodal method that combines textual cues and latent image representations from a domain-specific vision foundation model to georeference historical maps against contemporary geodata using keypoints and graph neural networks.

projects.title: Aesthetics of scientific data
projects.summary: Combine algorithmic techniques with state-of-the-art datasets to create critically articulated and aesthetically appealing visualizations of scientific data.

projects.title: Climate risk and nature-based solutions in humanitarian settings
projects.summary: Study climate risk and nature-based solutions in humanitarian settings, possibly in collaboration with MEDAIR using a geospatial inventory for Lebanon. The specific topic is still to be defined.

projects.title: Computational fluid dynamics for urban cooling
projects.summary: Study urban cooling with computational fluid dynamics.

projects.title: Impact of extreme heat on transport infrastructures
projects.summary: Assess changes in the frequency of future rail track buckling and other transport-related risks under heat, using the spatial and temporal distribution of transport infrastructure and temperature projections.

projects.title: Impact of weather on mobility
Investigating commuting patterns in Switzerland using mobility models
projects.summary: Analyse commuting flows in Switzerland using the Communal Matrix dataset, test existing mobility models such as those in the scikit-mobility package to predict flows, and compare results with other datasets such as Spanish mobility data.

projects.title: Machine Learning applications to urban sciences
projects.summary: Apply machine learning to urban climate prediction (temperature, humidity, wind speed), land use change over time, and mobility and urban growth.

projects.title: Modeling traffic flows
projects.summary: Describe traffic flows in cities using theories and approaches from fluid dynamics and porous media, based on existing high-resolution datasets.

projects.title: Modeling visitors–residents competition in overtourism
projects.summary: Model the competition between visitors and residents in overtourism.

projects.title: Modelling groundwater pollution & remediation
projects.summary: Simulate flow and transport processes in the subsurface to assess groundwater contamination at a selected site and explore remediation options.

projects.title: Modelling urban growth
projects.summary: Review the literature on the space-time evolution of urban areas, study feedbacks between population growth and urban transport networks, and test and adapt an existing urban growth model to explain complex urban dynamics with simple spatial rules.

projects.title: Monitoring and modeling urban CO2 fluxes
projects.summary: Test urban climate sensors (such as a flux tower at the UNIL campus, thermal cameras and drones), analyse the collected data, and/or develop an anthropogenic CO2 emissions model to compare observations with theoretical results.

projects.title: Predicting population changes in time and space
projects.summary: Develop a gravitational model to describe space-time variations in population density resulting from human mobility, from hourly to seasonal timescales.

projects.title: Stochastic modelling of urban climate
projects.summary: Develop a stochastic description of urban climate to characterise the space-time variability of urban surface and air temperature fields.

projects.title: Urban wind energy multiscale modeling
projects.summary: Ingest the swissBUILDING3D 3.0 high-resolution building morphology dataset into the PALM-4U CFD model to explore urban wind energy potential across major Swiss conurbations.

projects.title: A multiscale forecasting system for wind energy production
projects.summary: Use online observation data to validate WIRE's multiscale simulation system for forecasting wind and energy output from wind farms over complex terrain, applied as a case study to the JUVENT wind farm in the Jura mountains, Switzerland.

projects.title: Example 2: Wake characteristics of a wind farm sited in a multiscale rough topography
projects.summary: Wind tunnel experiments on a wind farm sited in a multiscale rough topography, comparing power performance and wake characteristics with an ideal flat terrain and benchmarking analytical wake models for prediction in such terrain.

projects.title: Example 4: Wind Energy Optimization
projects.summary: Master student project on optimizing wind energy projects by improving predictions of wind and turbulence around turbines and wind farms. Tasks include developing a virtual wind simulator (large-eddy simulation and simpler analytical models), field measurements with scanning LiDARs, and wind-tunnel experiments on wind farm layouts and turbine siting over complex terrain.

projects.title: Investigation of flow development in thermally-stratified turbulent boundary layers
projects.summary: Experimental study of how thermally stratified turbulent boundary layers develop in the WiRE boundary layer wind tunnel, under unstable, neutral and stable atmospheric-like temperature conditions and varying free stream velocities. The work includes pitot tube and thermocouple measurements, PIV feasibility tests, heat flux measurements, and power curve tests of a miniature wind turbine.

projects.title: Wind tunnel study of wind turbine performance and wind turbine wakes over complex terrain
projects.summary: Wind tunnel experiments will study the performance of wind turbines placed on idealized terrains such as cliffs and isolated hills, in order to optimize turbine placement on the landscape. The study also examines turbine wakes over complex terrain.

projects.title: Wind tunnel study on wind farm design optimization
projects.summary: Scaled-down wind turbine models will be used in a wind tunnel to study how turbulent boundary layer flow interacts with wind farms of different configurations and turbine densities. The goal is to optimize wind farm design by maximizing energy output and minimizing fatigue loads.

projects.title: Deep Learning image reconstruction of cones free-running cardiac MRI
projects.summary: Master's project in cardiovascular MRI on deep learning-based image reconstruction for free-running cardiac MRI acquired with cones trajectories. Based at CHUV Biopôle, Lausanne.

projects.title: Fast metabolic imaging by magnetic resonance fingerprinting
projects.summary: Master or semester project on fast metabolic imaging using magnetic resonance fingerprinting at EPFL CIBM, Lausanne.

projects.title: Functional magnetic resonance spectroscopy at 7 Tesla
projects.summary: Master or semester project on functional magnetic resonance spectroscopy at 7 Tesla at EPFL CIBM, Lausanne.

projects.title: Novel hardware technologies for neuroimaging and neurostimulation
projects.summary: Master or semester project on new hardware technologies for neuroimaging and neurostimulation at EPFL CIBM, Lausanne.

projects.title: Optimisation of the process pipeline of cerebrovascular reactivity data for clinical research
projects.summary: Master project to optimise the data processing pipeline for cerebrovascular reactivity MRI data used in clinical research. Located at HUG, CIBM MRI HUG-UNIGE, Geneva.

projects.title: 3D Contact Angle Measurements and Image Analysis in Solid-Oxide Cell Materials
projects.summary: Measure 3D contact angles and analyse images of solid-oxide cell materials.

projects.title: 3D skin tissue analysis
projects.summary: Analyse three-dimensional skin tissue imaging data.

projects.title: Bringing deep-denoising into X-ray CT reconstruction
projects.summary: Integrate deep-learning denoising into X-ray computed tomography reconstruction.

projects.title: Deep Learning System for Automated Segmentation and Object Classification in Scientific images
projects.summary: Develop a deep learning system that automatically segments and classifies objects in scientific images.

projects.title: Dynamic wetting measurement with image analysis on synchrotron x-ray tomography data
projects.summary: Measure dynamic wetting using image analysis applied to synchrotron X-ray tomography data.

projects.title: Event detection by signal processing to characterize optical fiber
projects.summary: Detect events in optical fiber signals using signal processing to characterize the fiber.

projects.title: Improving Segment Anything (SAM) output with Spline-Based Contour Editing
projects.summary: Improve the output of the Segment Anything model by editing its segmentation contours with spline-based methods.

projects.title: Interactive Visualization of Scientific Image Datasets
projects.summary: Build interactive tools to visualize large scientific image datasets.

projects.title: Learning Molecular Anisotropic Diffusion with Self-Supervised Deep Learning
projects.summary: Learn molecular anisotropic diffusion from imaging data using self-supervised deep learning.

projects.title: Python software development for automated single-cell protein isolation with a CryoWriter
projects.summary: Develop Python software to automate single-cell protein isolation with a CryoWriter instrument.

projects.title: Semester Project: X-ray reconstruction corrections for mechanics and biology
projects.summary: Develop corrections for X-ray image reconstruction for applications in mechanics and biology.

projects.title: AI and Agentic Driven Generation of State-of-the-Art Branch Predictors
projects.summary: Use AI and agentic methods to automatically generate state-of-the-art branch predictors for processors.

projects.title: Learning Atmospheric Similarity for Retrieval-Augmented Weather Forecasting
projects.summary: Learn atmospheric similarity to retrieve relevant past states for retrieval-augmented weather forecasting.

projects.title: MSc thesis: Evaluating explainable machine learning tools for understanding greenhouse gas flux time series
projects.summary: Evaluate explainable machine learning tools for interpreting greenhouse gas flux time series.

projects.title: MSc thesis: Uncertainty-aware deep learning for large-scale mapping of mass movements using SAR interferometry
projects.summary: Develop uncertainty-aware deep learning to map mass movements at large scale from SAR interferometry data.

projects.title: Post-Training Quantization of Weather Foundation Models: Attention Quantization and Long-Rollout Calibration
projects.summary: Apply post-training quantization to weather foundation models, focusing on attention quantization and calibration over long rollouts.

projects.title: Semester Project or Master Thesis: Flow Matching for Imaging Inverse Problems with Nonlinear Forward Operators
projects.summary: Develop flow matching generative models to solve imaging inverse problems with nonlinear forward operators. The work is aimed at image reconstruction.

projects.title: Synthetic Data Generation and Quality Assessment for the Mountain Biodiversity Knowledge Graph
projects.summary: Generate synthetic data for the Mountain Biodiversity Knowledge Graph and assess the quality of that data. The work applies NLP methods.

projects.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Therapy Planning and Design
projects.summary: Topic is the use of generative AI to support planning and design of therapies.

projects.title: Large-Scale Frontier Model for High-Dimensional Biological Imaging Data
projects.summary: Topic is building a large-scale frontier model for analysing high-dimensional biological imaging data.

projects.title: Reasoning in Biological Foundation Models
projects.summary: Topic is studying how reasoning can be performed in foundation models for biology.

projects.title: Vision-Language Models for Biomedicine
projects.summary: Topic is the development of vision-language models applied to biomedical data.

projects.title: AI agents that foster learners' critical thinking through argumentation
projects.summary: Student project on AI agents designed to foster learners' critical thinking through argumentation.

projects.title: Designing real-time AI support for collaborative, inquiry-based science learning
projects.summary: Student project on designing real-time AI support for collaborative, inquiry-based science learning.

projects.title: Human-AI co-orchestration of group collaborative argumentation and ideation
projects.summary: Student project on human-AI co-orchestration to support group collaborative argumentation and ideation.

projects.title: Human-AI interactions that preserve and elevate human expertise in AI-augmented work
projects.summary: Student project on designing human-AI interactions that preserve and elevate human expertise in AI-augmented work.

projects.title: Interactive tools to prepare citizens for democratic deliberation and policy co-creation
projects.summary: Student project on interactive tools that help citizens prepare for democratic deliberation and policy co-creation.

projects.title: Participatory and community-based approaches to AI development
projects.summary: Student project on participatory and community-based approaches to AI development.

projects.title: Worker-centred design of workplace AI systems
projects.summary: Student project on designing workplace AI systems centred on the needs of workers.

projects.title: Optimization, Formalization and Benchmarking
projects.summary: Projects on optimization, formalization and benchmarking of proof system components and techniques, which can be tailored to the student's experience and interests.

projects.title: Zero knowledge succinct arguments, probabilistic proofs and complexity theory
projects.summary: Projects on zero knowledge succinct arguments, probabilistic proofs and complexity theory, which can be tailored to the student's experience and interests.

projects.title: 3D Surface reconstruction using 3D Gaussians and SDF
projects.summary: The project explores building primitives so that a surface can be extracted from a 3D Gaussian Splatting scene with minimal extra computation, comparing ad-hoc approaches with neural SDFs trained alongside the Gaussians. Expected work includes a literature review and experiments with different SDF formulations.

projects.title: Applied Deep Learning for Computer Aided Engineering
projects.summary: Students work on one of several CAE problems addressed with deep learning, such as object geometry modelling and parameterization, physical performance evaluation with surrogate models, and gradient-based optimization, applied to aeronautics engineering in collaboration with ISAE-SUPAERO.

projects.title: Computer Vision for Waste Management (CVLAB x Wasteflow)
projects.summary: Develop a computer vision solution for WasteFlow's recycling facility service, covering real-time detection and classification of waste on conveyor belts, efficiency measurement, mass estimation, and purity assessment of sorted output. Edge deployment of models is also of interest.

projects.title: Efficient Diffusion Models via Quantization and Compression
projects.summary: Explore and systematically evaluate quantization and compression methods (INT8/INT4, mixed-precision, pruning, low-rank factorization, distillation) for diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion, to reduce computational and memory requirements while preserving generative quality.

projects.title: Interpretable and Controllable Neural Shape Parameterizations
projects.summary: Build on DeepGeo, a neural network and mesh-based deformation approach for 2D and 3D shapes, to develop methods that make neural shape parameterizations more interpretable, controllable, and efficient to optimize. Possible directions include automatically finding parameter directions tied to geometric properties such as airfoil thickness, camber, or wing twist.

projects.title: Real-Time 3D Tracking and Anomaly Detection for Maritime Kite Systems
projects.summary: Extend a vision system that tracks an automated maritime kite wing from 2D to 3D by integrating and calibrating a second camera for stereovision. The work also moves the previous ROS-simulated pipeline to a real-time hardware system and develops anomaly detection, such as tears, abnormal trajectories and wing shape estimation, linked to emergency control actions.

projects.title: Recovering Thin Structures in 3D Foundation Models
projects.summary: 3D foundation models based on feed-forward transformers reconstruct scene geometry and camera parameters, but they perform poorly on thin structures because of coarse patchification. The project investigates how to improve the performance of such models (illustrated with Depth Anything 3) on thin structures.

projects.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Flight Dynamics
projects.summary: The project explores self-supervised methods, such as Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA), to learn how an aircraft responds to control inputs from sensor measurements. The goal is to make the learned dynamics models useful for control, with tests on simulated flight data and possibly real measurements from the lab's experimental aircraft.

projects.title: Structured 3D Shape Optimization with Part-Based Implicit Neural Representations
projects.summary: Extend a part-based implicit neural representation (PartSDF) to engineering-driven 3D shape representation and optimization under physical and design constraints, such as aerodynamics or structural efficiency. The work also targets scalable learning for many-part objects without invalid outputs.

projects.title: Accelerating Safe ML Systems
projects.summary: Investigate how to use Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) to build machine learning systems that are both fast and secure for distributed training of large models.

projects.title: Distributed Resource Efficient Inference Engine
projects.summary: Work on the distributed inference engine Anyd, which aggregates heterogeneous hardware into a unified cluster that automatically schedules generative AI inference and handles failures transparently.

projects.title: Scalable Distributed Cache Coherency
projects.summary: Design scalable distributed cache coherence protocols that keep shared data consistent across cached copies while reducing the communication overhead that limits current protocols.

projects.title: LARS Audio Processing
projects.summary: Add audio capabilities to the LARS system, including computing hardware delays and extracting audio features such as beat tracking and key finding. The project targets low-latency real-time processing.

projects.title: LARS Performance Optimization & Benchmarking
projects.summary: Profile the LARS real-time music system to find bottlenecks, optimise C++ code paths and threading/concurrency, and build benchmarking tools with automated performance regression tests. The goal is to improve real-time performance and scalability.

projects.title: LARS Python Utilities to C++ Core Migration
projects.summary: Move key Python utilities of the LARS music system to optimised modern C++, keeping Python bindings via nanobind. The project also contributes to a C++ version of the pattern language used for algorithmic composition in LARS.

projects.title: LARS Testing & Quality Assurance (C++ & Python)
projects.summary: Build a comprehensive test suite (unit, integration, regression and load tests) for the C++ and Python components of the LARS real-time interactive music system, and set up automated CI testing workflows. The goal is to improve the reliability and maintainability of LARS.

projects.title: Perceptual abilities of musical experts
projects.summary: Replicate existing behavioural music perception experiments with top-level performing artists to compare their perceptual abilities with those of non-musicians and typical musicians. The project involves critically updating the methods, implementing an online version of the experiment, and analysing the data.

projects.title: Web development for graphic music analysis app
projects.summary: Rewrite the serverless web app for reductive music analysis in type-safe code with a modern event-driven JavaScript framework, or develop features and fix bugs in the existing legacy code base. The app lets researchers express music analyses as graphs embedded in MEI music scores.

projects.title: Coercion-resistant proof of personhood as a foundation for digital democracy
projects.summary: Prototype, test, and evaluate a coercion-resistance mechanism for remote e-voting in the context of in-person pseudonym parties, which authenticate real humans while limiting vote buying and coercion. The project includes building a usable app mockup, running a volunteer user study, and writing a report that could lead to a publication.
skills: communication with volunteers and administrative authorities

projects.title: Paradox-resistant reasoning in automated theorem provers
projects.summary: Formalize, validate, and metalogically reason about Grounded Deduction, a non-classical logic foundation that allows unrestricted recursive definitions while defusing semantic paradoxes such as the Liar and Yablo's paradox. The work uses a proof assistant or automated theorem prover such as Isabelle, Coq, or Lean, and may extend to a grounded set theory in the LISA prover.

projects.title: Writing and editing tools based on matchertext and MinML
projects.summary: Develop tools around MinML, an experimental markup language based on the matchertext syntactic discipline that is a more readable alternative to HTML/XML. Possible work includes refining the language, integrating MinML into authoring tools, and designing a LaTeX-like MinML for document authoring.

projects.title: 3D Question Answering at City-Scale: Multimodal LLMs
projects.summary: Implement a multimodal LLM for question answering over city-scale 3D models, build a city-scale 3D QA benchmark from historical data, and integrate the system into the Time Atlas.

projects.title: Analysing Layout Elements of Historical Maps
projects.summary: Detect map layout elements such as cartouches, scale bars and legends in a dataset of about 400,000 historical maps and analyse their similarity and clustering across authors, regions and periods.

projects.title: Annotation of Culture-Specific Data for LLM Evaluation Using the Psychosocial Categorisation Model (PSCM)
projects.summary: Create a bilingual (Armenian-English) culturally annotated dataset using the PSCM schema and use it to evaluate LLM and MT performance on culture-specific meaning.

projects.title: Armenian Epigraphy and Cultural Heritage Data Analysis
projects.summary: Collect and clean books on Armenian epigraphy and cultural heritage, build a database, and extract key terms and themes with NLP techniques.

projects.title: ArmEpiC: AI-Assisted Authority Files & Validation Dashboard
projects.summary: Develop AI-assisted workflows to enrich authority files for the Armenian epigraphic corpus and build a validation dashboard.

projects.title: ArmEpiC: Armenian Editorial Signs Converter
projects.summary: Build a converter that transforms Armenian editorial signs in the epigraphic corpus into standardised representations.

projects.title: ArmEpiC: EpiDoc Corpus Creation & Geolocation
projects.summary: Transform the IndiaArmEpiC corpus of Armenian inscriptions from India (based on EAP1721) into a structured TEI/EpiDoc dataset and geolocate its entries.

projects.title: ArmEpiC: Standalone Web Visualisation
projects.summary: Create a standalone web tool to visualise and analyse the Armenian epigraphic corpus.

projects.title: Bias analysis of cultural heritage manipulation classification of Wikipedia edits by LLMs
projects.summary: Analyse biases of open-source LLMs when classifying Wikipedia edits on Armenian and Ukrainian cultural heritage as manipulative, compare against human labels, and explore simple bias mitigation strategies.

projects.title: Biology of a VLM: Transcoder Training for Multimodal Interpretability
projects.summary: Train a transcoder replacement model for a vision-language model and use it to study concept representations and reasoning steps in the model's internals.

projects.title: Converging Conceptual Abstraction in Self-Supervised Models
projects.summary: Develop a representation convergence measure that compares the conceptual abstractions learned by sparse autoencoders or transcoders across self-supervised vision models.

projects.title: Data Visualization Dashboard for Monitoring and Quality Control of Large-Scale Data Processing
projects.summary: Implement a modular, lightweight dashboard that shows the stages and quality of the Impresso data processing pipeline and deploy it online.

projects.title: Dense Language Encoders for Agglomerative Models
projects.summary: Build a dense text encoder aligned with EUPE dense features (similar to Talk2DINO) to enable zero-shot open-vocabulary semantic segmentation with agglomerative vision models.

projects.title: Detection, Linking, and Georeferencing of Place Names in Historical Newspapers
projects.summary: Scale multilingual location detection and georeferencing, with a focus on sub-city levels, across the Impresso historical newspaper corpus.

projects.title: Discovering Historical Events Through Spatio-Temporal Analysis
projects.summary: Design a reproducible pipeline that detects historically significant intersections of time and place in the Flickr Commons archive, in collaboration with the Flickr Foundation, using unsupervised anomaly detection.

projects.title: Driving Representation Convergence using Image Aesthetics
projects.summary: Test whether aesthetic images produce distinct or more convergent representations across vision models, using aesthetics datasets and an internationally and historically balanced dataset.

projects.title: EPFL Digital Twin Foundation Model
projects.summary: Prototype a foundation model of the EPFL campus by aligning datasets from the Urban Digital Twin ecosystem (buildings, mobility, food, schedules) into a unified spatiotemporal representation for forecasting and simulation.

projects.title: Evaluating the Novelty of Knowledge in Texts with Large Language Models
projects.summary: Develop algorithms that assess whether textual sources contain knowledge that was not present in the training data of open-source LLMs, with applications to historical research.

projects.title: Exploring Large Vision Models for Historical Newspaper Segmentation
projects.summary: Evaluate large vision models for segmenting and labelling logical layout units (articles, headlines, tables, images) on historical newspaper pages from the Impresso corpus.

projects.title: Exploring the structure of the Venetian urban fabric with 3-dimensional isovists
projects.summary: Analyse the structure of Venetian urban space using three-dimensional isovists.

projects.title: Geolocating Artworks
projects.summary: Use vision-language models and multimodal embeddings to identify the places depicted in paintings, engravings and illustrations, and link artworks to spatial entities in the Time Atlas.

projects.title: Identification and Classification of Maps in Historical Newspapers
projects.summary: Train image classifiers to detect maps in historical newspaper pages and to classify the country or region each map represents.

projects.title: IIIF Document Information Extraction for Time Atlas
projects.summary: Build a pipeline that retrieves manuscript images via IIIF, processes them with language-vision models to extract text, layout and named entities, and prepares structured data for the Time Atlas.

projects.title: Mapping Newspapers: Creation of a database of Swiss historical newspapers based on Blaser's bibliography
projects.summary: Extract semi-structured information from Fritz Blaser's Swiss Press Bibliography (PDF) into a lightweight database documenting Swiss newspapers from 1803 to 1958.

projects.title: News Articles in Space and Time
projects.summary: A project on analysing news articles along spatial and temporal dimensions, as named in the title. No detailed description is published yet.

projects.title: Pleiades Integration into the TimeAtlas
projects.summary: Design and prototype the integration of the Pleiades gazetteer of ancient places into the Time Atlas infrastructure, including data mapping and ingestion pipelines.

projects.title: Preparing and Evaluating Vintage Language Models
projects.summary: Build the methodological and technical foundations for language models trained only on historical corpora, studying contamination control, chronological training pipelines, and historically grounded evaluation benchmarks.

projects.title: Preparing Historical Data for Apertus
projects.summary: Collect, filter, clean and document historical corpora (books, newspapers, archives) to prepare training material for a future training cycle of the open Apertus language model.

projects.title: Projecting Representations of Beauty
projects.summary: Build a pseudo-labelling pipeline that projects image aesthetic assessment labels onto 3D scenes and distil a model that predicts aesthetic labels from point cloud structure.

projects.title: Reconstructing the Past: Generating 3D Models of Lost Buildings from Stylistically Diverse Inputs with Geometry Transformers
projects.summary: Test and fine-tune feed-forward geometry transformers on stylised historical images to generate 3D models of destroyed or lost buildings from the DHLAB's historical image collections.

projects.title: Reconstructing the topology of Venetian domestic space through cadastral analysis
projects.summary: Reconstruct the topology of domestic space in Venice by analysing cadastral records.

projects.title: Semi-automated historical GIS construction for Venetian secondary sources
projects.summary: Semi-automatically build a historical GIS from Venetian secondary sources.

projects.title: Spatial Intelligence at Scale: Hierarchical Reconstruction
projects.summary: Investigate object-part hierarchies in city-scale 3D data derived from open-vocabulary point labels, including hyperbolic embeddings for hierarchical scene representations.

projects.title: Spatial Intelligence at Scale: Human Interaction
projects.summary: Design user interfaces for querying and manipulating large-scale 3D scenes with multimodal queries, including 3D-native search and retrieval-augmented chat with MLLMs, within the Time Atlas.

projects.title: Spatial Intelligence at Scale: Implicit Reconstruction
projects.summary: Support training of an open-vocabulary model for city-scale 3D scenes by preparing datasets and extending the Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer toward egocentric semantic understanding.

projects.title: Tarot Deck Motif Analysis
projects.summary: Prepare the computational analysis of visual motifs across historical Tarot decks: corpus collection, motif taxonomy, and prototype detection and classification tools.

projects.title: Temporal Language Models and the Dynamics of Language Change
projects.summary: Extend temporal language modelling approaches inspired by TLM-1 to analyse semantic drift, narrative evolution and forecasting of linguistic change in diachronic corpora.

projects.title: The Social Life of Images: Using Social Metadata to Enhance AI Generated Descriptions of Digital Image Archives
projects.summary: Develop and evaluate methods that combine vision models with social metadata (tags, comments, galleries) from Flickr Commons to produce richer descriptions of historical archival images.

projects.title: Tracking the Weaponization and Manipulation of Cultural Heritage in Armenia
projects.summary: Retrieve and analyse Wikipedia editing histories, talk pages and related sources to monitor manipulation of Armenian cultural heritage narratives.

projects.title: Tracking the Weaponization and Manipulation of Cultural Heritage in Ukraine by Russia
projects.summary: Analyse Wikipedia editing histories, talk pages and related sources to monitor manipulation of Ukrainian cultural heritage narratives.

projects.title: Typological analysis of Venetian floor plans through Computer Vision
projects.summary: Use computer vision to conduct a typological analysis of Venetian floor plans.

projects.title: VLM Finetuning for Accurate Features from Images of Degraded Point Clouds
projects.summary: Evaluate the gap between real and synthetic (point cloud) images for vision-language models and fine-tune them to produce accurate semantic features from synthetic renderings of 3D scenes.

projects.title: What's in those millions of images? Generating accurate descriptions for 4 million historical newspaper images
projects.summary: Evaluate and apply vision-language models to generate accurate multilingual captions for historical newspaper images, and define an evaluation method for description quality.

projects.title: World Model Semantic Surprise as a Measure for Multimodal Urban Incongruity
projects.summary: Develop embedding-space semantic trajectory tools and apply them to urban trajectories from driving videos, street-view imagery, LiDAR or text to measure how incongruous parts of the built environment are.

projects.title: Cost models & tuning the query optimizer of a JIT analytical engine
projects.summary: The student learns Apache Calcite and builds cost models for the operators of Proteus, an in-house analytical DBMS engine, then extends them to parallelism and resource allocation. The project also includes an auto-tuning infrastructure to select cost-model hyper-parameters for different machines.

projects.title: Efficient Concurrent Interval Container for Multicore Systems
projects.summary: Design and implement a concurrent interval container, inspired by the Boost Interval Container Library, that supports overlap and containment queries and atomic updates that may split, merge, or aggregate intervals. The prototype is to be evaluated against a sequential container under a global lock and against concurrent-index baselines.

projects.title: Limiting interference of code generation to analytical query execution through remote JIT-ing
projects.summary: The project studies how just-in-time code generation interferes with analytical query execution in a DBMS, and proposes running code generation remotely on a separate machine to isolate it. The student will benchmark the interference, use LLVM remote JIT, and modify the Proteus engine to allow a low-footprint version to run on a low-end machine.

projects.title: Memory-Aware Hash Joins for Heterogeneous Memory Environments
projects.summary: The project studies the design space of hash join implementations in heterogeneous memory environments such as CXL memory. The student evaluates existing state-of-the-art hash joins, analyzes the design space, and proposes memory-aware design choices evaluated on SSB and TPC-H.

projects.title: Understanding and Mitigating Real-World Global Serializability Violations
projects.summary: The project studies global serializability violations in multi-database transactions of microservice applications. The student empirically analyses 2-3 open-source microservice applications, then integrates existing mitigation methods (such as Sonata and the Ticket method) and evaluates their performance.

projects.title: Extracting Block I/O Stream Representations from Filesystems
projects.summary: Investigate how filesystems such as ext4, XFS, F2FS or Btrfs transform application file operations into block I/O, and derive a minimal set of block I/O streams that captures the steady-state, SSD-relevant behavior and write amplification of each filesystem-mediated workload.

projects.title: Profiling Automated Verifiers
projects.summary: Build a profiler that attributes SMT-based verifier solving time (e.g., Dafny, KLEE) across the verifier stack, distinguishes useful from useless work and brute-force search from precise reasoning, and evaluates it on real verifier performance issues.

projects.title: SSD-Aware RL for Data Placement in Storage Systems
projects.summary: Reproduce a reinforcement-learning data-placement baseline on heterogeneous SSDs and extend the agent with SSD-internal signals (garbage collection, write amplification, utilization, wear) and rewards that balance performance, write amplification and wear.

projects.title: Beyond the Strings: LLM-Based Knowledge Extraction for Historical Puppetry Knowledge Graphs
projects.summary: Evaluate LLM-based extraction of historical relationships and scholarly interpretations from theatrical and archival texts about Sophie Taeuber-Arp's König Hirsch marionettes, producing structured data for knowledge graph integration under a predefined ontology.

projects.title: Evaluation Framework for Cross-Domain Visual Retrieval in Cultural Heritage Image Collections
projects.summary: Develop a reproducible evaluation framework for cross-domain visual retrieval and visualization tools applied to cultural heritage image collections, including the Murten Panorama and 15th-century illuminated manuscripts. The work covers dataset survey, construction of evaluation sets with generative AI, and metric definition.

projects.title: Generative Workflow for Navigable 3D Worlds from a Large-Scale Panoramic Painting
projects.summary: Develop a reproducible generative AI workflow that turns segments of the 360° Murten Panorama painting into navigable 3D scenes for VR/XR, combining world models and 3D asset generation and placing scenes on a geolocated map.
skills: generative AI tools for images and 3D

projects.title: Computational Design with Multiple Tension Elements: Elastic Cables and Sheets with Elastic Rod Structures
projects.summary: The project studies how elastic rods held in target curves by cables and sheet patches can be designed with both kinds of tension elements combined and interchangeable. The student will develop methods for form-finding cable-patch configurations, evaluating and comparing designs, intersection-free layout, and topology optimization under constraints, building on the existing Tencer inverse design and cable-to-patch pipelines.

projects.title: Inverse design of highly curved surfaces for surface-based inflatables
projects.summary: Develop a parameterization method for highly curved surfaces that respects the contraction bounds of surface-based inflatables, using cone singularities to keep the scale factors within physically realizable limits. The project asks how cone placement and angles can be optimized, how the resulting cuts can be realized physically, and how much this extends the achievable shapes.

projects.title: Simulation and Design of Transformable Elastic Linkages
projects.summary: Study and simulate how elastic beams and joints can be designed and connected to achieve desired transformations, shapes, and functions, building on deployable systems such as X-Shells, C-Shells and BamX. The project can explore new deployable linkage designs guided by geometric insight and numerical simulation.

projects.title: Tencer Metamaterials: Unit Cell Generation and Rigid Motion Analysis
projects.summary: The project aims to build an automatic tool that generates diverse candidate unit-cell topologies built from tencers (tension-constrained elastic rods), for systematic exploration of metamaterial designs. It also seeks a strategy to refine these designs so that no undesired relative rigid motion between components is possible, yielding a database of interesting designs.

projects.title: Improving Coverage Reliability in Cortex-M Firmware Rehosting
projects.summary: Studies how the approximations of Cortex-M firmware rehosting systems affect the reliability of coverage reported by fuzzing, and records coverage together with execution context. The project then aims to develop techniques that improve coverage-guided fuzzing of rehosted Cortex-M firmware.

projects.title: Ownership-Aware Bug Hunting in Rust Crates
projects.summary: Aims to build an ownership-aware bug detection mechanism for Rust crates that models ownership transitions induced by unsafe APIs, in order to find bugs such as double-frees that the compiler cannot enforce. The project targets nested or recursive types where bitwise copies share heap allocations.

projects.title: Accelerating ecological connectivity analysis with graph neural networks
projects.summary: Develop graph neural network methods that learn coarse graph embeddings of fine-scale landscape features, to make resistance-distance gene flow predictions for ecological connectivity computationally tractable. Directions include graph coarsening strategies, approximation error bounds, and validation on ecological datasets.

projects.title: Finding Slow Components in a Graph
projects.summary: Study how many random shortest-path distance queries are needed to identify a set of vertices V_1 with much larger exponential edge weights in a weighted graph, and how the query strategy (adaptive or non-adaptive) affects this. The work includes literature review, simulations, and theoretical accuracy bounds.

projects.title: High-performance differentiable AMG in JAX with GPU acceleration
projects.summary: Develop an algebraic multigrid (AMG) solver in JAX that supports automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration, for use in scientific machine learning workflows that need differentiable iterative linear solves. The work involves analysing existing pyAMG and AMG.jl implementations and designing an architecture compatible with JAX's functional and just-in-time compilation model.

projects.title: Reusable Foundations for Probabilistic Proofs in Lean
projects.summary: Develop reusable foundations in Lean, on top of Mathlib, for probability theory (Markov chains, random walks, couplings) so that probabilists can formalize their results more easily. If time allows, the library will be used to formalize a paper on random graphs and branching processes.

projects.title: Dataset Acquisition for Low-Light Image Denoising
projects.summary: Build a new dataset of clean-noisy image pairs and dark calibration frames captured at many exposure times, to extend the 2-Shots in the Dark low-light denoising method to a wider range of exposure times and sensor temperatures. The student captures, organizes and preprocesses the data, then publishes it on Hugging Face with a dataset card. All acquisition equipment is provided by the lab.
skills: Basics of image and signal processing
DSLR shooting in manual mode (ISO, exposure time)

projects.title: Accelerate FPGA Implementation Time
projects.summary: Reduce the long FPGA implementation time, from several minutes to a few seconds, needed to generate the bitstream from high-level synthesis designs.

projects.title: Hardware coherence on various wishbone bus-architectures
projects.summary: Investigate hardware cache coherence protocols (such as MSI and MESI) for Wishbone shared, crossbar and ring bus architectures, and propose and implement software-configurable coherence protocols on a Hazard3 RISC-V CPU system.

projects.title: Low-Level Optimization of Dynamically Scheduled Circuits
projects.summary: Improve performance of dynamically scheduled circuits by optimising the RTL-to-FPGA implementation stage, including logic synthesis and place-and-route in Vivado, to account for physical constraints such as routing delays and congestion.

projects.title: Open-Source Work on Dynamic High-level Synthesis Compiler Targeting FPGAs
projects.summary: Contribute to Dynamatic, an open-source dynamic high-level synthesis compiler built on MLIR that generates RTL for FPGAs from C/C++. Possible work includes compiler passes at different lowering stages, and debugging, visualisation or benchmarking tools, with contributions meant to become part of the codebase.

projects.title: Optimizing place and route for high frequency task parallel FPGA accelerators
projects.summary: Analyse the frequency of circuits generated by the open-source HardCilk task-parallel scheduler on FPGAs using Vivado place and route, and test whether adding elastic buffers to ready-valid interfaces increases the design frequency.

projects.title: Postquantum Cryptography Core Using High-Level Synthesis
projects.summary: Explore and improve the quality of results of post-quantum cryptography hardware cores generated with high-level synthesis from C/C++, compared with RTL-based designs.

projects.title: SOC-graphical configurator as VS-code plug-in
projects.summary: Build a VS Code plugin that provides a graphical tool for designing System-on-Chip architectures from OpenRisc-based softcore modules, for use in the CS-473 and CS-476 courses, with export of designs as TikZ pictures and PDF.

projects.title: Toward Coarse-Grained Field Programmable Gate Arrays
projects.summary: Study a coarser-grained version of FPGAs and evaluate its performance as a word-level reconfigurable computing fabric, including new compiler optimisations, architectural ideas, and physical implementation and modelling.

projects.title: A Digital Twin for collective decision making
projects.summary: Build and extend a Digital Twin that replicates zebrafish behaviour in response to virtual conspecifics, starting with an auto-regressive generative model baseline and then using interpretable approaches to explain decision making. The aim is to make predictions that could be tested in real animals.

projects.title: Implementing and extending a biologically inspired computational model of spatial navigation in rodents
projects.summary: Implement a computational model of a virtual rat navigating environments, combining a taxon pathway (visual input to motor actions) and a locale pathway (grid and place cells). The model is to be validated in reorientation and water-maze paradigms and then extended.

projects.title: Modeling perceptual rules of social interactions in single animal virtual reality
projects.summary: Use computational modelling and machine learning to test whether zebrafish visual preference for virtual fish-like motion stems from hard-wired tuning to average motion statistics or from an idiosyncratic coupling to the fish's own swim cycle. Models will be fitted to existing behavioural recordings and possibly extended to predict neural signals.

projects.title: Training spiking networks to generate fast time-varying patterns
projects.summary: Aims to train networks of spiking SRM0 neurons with escape noise, using FORCE-style online learning and exact population rate equations, to produce fast and complex time-varying activity patterns. The project examines how far the approach extends as the speed of network dynamics is no longer constrained.

projects.title: When is a good predictor a good model?
projects.summary: Investigates which model-brain comparison metrics (linear predictivity, representational similarity analysis, CKA) can identify artificial networks that truly share the brain's mechanisms rather than merely predicting neural activity. The student records from networks with known shared or different mechanisms and tests whether lesion effects transfer between candidate model and target system.

projects.title: Message passing for quantum models (SMILS)
projects.summary: Develop message passing techniques for simple quantum spin models on graphs, using functional integral and/or discrete phase space representations, with a focus on investigating topological phases.

projects.title: Quantum constraint satisfaction problems (SMILS)
projects.summary: The project investigates quantum versions of constraint satisfaction problems such as quantum K-SAT, aiming to determine the phase diagram as a function of constraint density and to find product-state ground states (PRODSAT phase) with algorithmic methods. It starts from a study of the basic literature on the topic.

projects.title: Universal prediction and alpha-mutual information
projects.summary: The project studies Alpha-NML predictors, a class of estimators interpolating between the Krichevsky-Trofimov (KT) and Normalized Maximum Likelihood (NML) estimators for universal prediction under log loss. Students would run experimental work (MATLAB or Python) to extend closed-form gamma-function formulas to longer sequences, derive formulas for non-i.i.d. sources such as Markov sources, and assess average-case performance compared with KT and NML.

projects.title: Analysing the Effect of Assistant Post-Training on Diversity and Sycophancy in Pedagogical LLMs
projects.summary: Studies how diversity, sycophancy and safety change across the post-training stages (base, SFT, DPO, RLVR) of the open model Olmo 3 7B when generating feedback on open-ended student work. The project aims to find internal features linked to these behaviours and to test lightweight interventions (weight interpolation, feature steering, short LoRA fine-tuning) that improve diversity and reduce sycophancy without undermining safety.

projects.title: Do Questions Trigger Misconceptions? Measuring When Student Misconceptions Show Up
projects.summary: Uses existing anonymised Eedi diagnostic maths responses to measure the trigger strength of each question-misconception pair and test whether it predicts when a student's misconception reappears, controlling for ability and difficulty. It also compares a persona-prompted open LLM simulator (e.g. Qwen3-8B) with real students' misconception rates.

projects.title: Mapping Failures of AI Agents on Educational Tasks
projects.summary: Analyses a dataset of agent interactions across six learning contexts to map failures of agentic AI systems on education tasks (understanding the learning context and modelling learner data) to generic failure taxonomies. The goal is to develop an education-specific coding scheme, combine manual and LLM-based trace analysis, and identify where existing taxonomies need refinement.

projects.title: Robustness of LLM Reasoning Strategies for Educational Applications
projects.summary: Investigates how different reasoning strategies (linear, symbolic, reflective, iterative) affect the robustness and reliability of LLMs under controlled perturbations in educational tasks such as misconception detection and educational content generation. It evaluates accuracy, explanation consistency, error propagation, recovery and the trade-off with computational cost.

projects.title: Comparing Representational Hierarchies in Neural Networks
projects.summary: Investigates whether neural networks learn similar representations across their full layer hierarchies, rather than only at individually matched layers. The project aims to develop a principled comparison method and reassess evidence for representational convergence across pretrained multi-modal models.

projects.title: Improving agents for single-cell genomics and biomedical discovery
projects.summary: Aims to improve the reasoning capabilities of LLM-based agents for single-cell biology tasks through agentic reinforcement learning, so that they can formulate hypotheses, design validation strategies and execute computational workflows.

projects.title: Learning patient-level predictions from the spatial proteome
projects.summary: Develops a multiple instance learning approach that aggregates single-cell, niche and tissue-level information from spatial proteomics data to predict patient-level outcomes such as cancer survival. The project evaluates performance versus training cohort size and whether model attention agrees with known pathology.

projects.title: What Do Language Models Need from 3D Encoders?
projects.summary: Studies what 3D encoders (point clouds or Gaussian splats) contribute when connected to a language model, and how 3D representations could be learned to be more useful for LLMs reasoning about 3D scenes. The question is also extended to modeling spatial organization of cells.

projects.title: AI safety evaluations feeding back into Apertus Posttraining
projects.summary: Work with UN agencies such as UNICC to incorporate findings from recent red-teaming studies into the posttraining recipes (safety SFT and RL) of the next generation Apertus model.

projects.title: Build decentralized LLMs in the browser
projects.summary: Practical project joining a larger team effort to build decentralized and federated training software in which many clients (e.g. phones or hospitals) collaboratively train models such as smaller LLMs while preserving data privacy; students would help integrate the Burn framework within DISCO.

projects.title: Communication-efficient gossip methods for replacing all-reduce in distributed LLM training
projects.summary: Implement decentralized pairwise averaging of model weights instead of all-to-all communication, and investigate how model and data parallelism settings and communication compression affect distributed LLM pre-training.

projects.title: Data curation and curriculum learning for pre-training, theory and practice
projects.summary: Semester project around LLM pre-training, covering data curation and curriculum learning, with both theoretical and practical components. Part of the MLO large language model project offer.

projects.title: Efficiency engineering for LLM pretraining and specifically MoE architectures
projects.summary: Semester project on improving the computational efficiency of LLM pre-training, with a focus on mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Improving factuality understanding for LLM training
projects.summary: Add a factuality tag or masking to each document to guide an LLM's understanding of what is factual, with the goal of enhancing factuality and reducing hallucinations; post-training techniques may also be investigated.

projects.title: Learning to sample on the fly for SGD / curriculum learning
projects.summary: Train an auxiliary network that assigns scores to training data points and use these scores to select an improved set of training points, exploring several ways of training the auxiliary parameters.

projects.title: LLM inference on old V100 GPUs
projects.summary: Aims to run recent large open-weight MoE models efficiently on the EPFL cluster of V100 GPUs and compare with newer GPU versions, applying quantization and communication-efficient parallelism with inference frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang in multi-GPU settings.

projects.title: LLM Pretraining Data Curation
projects.summary: Advance pre-training data curation beyond baselines such as FineWeb-2 HQ through new techniques for signal extraction, semantic filtering and partially synthetic augmentation or rephrasing, in English or multilingual settings. One idea is to study the impact of data quality on the curse of multilinguality and its relation to scaling laws.

projects.title: Novel architectures (including efficient long context or MoE related mechanisms)
projects.summary: Semester project on new LLM architectures, including efficient long-context and mixture-of-experts mechanisms. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Optimization dynamics for LLMs (e.g. Muon and AdEMAmix variants, and interactions with architecture)
projects.summary: Semester project studying optimization dynamics of LLM training, such as Muon and AdEMAmix variants and their interaction with architecture. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Safety and alignment during pretraining
projects.summary: Semester project on integrating safety and alignment considerations into LLM pre-training. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Scaling to longer context windows through modifications of attention
projects.summary: Semester project on extending the context length of LLMs by modifying the attention mechanism. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Tools-usage during pretraining & finetuning
projects.summary: Semester project on enabling tool usage by LLMs during pre-training and fine-tuning. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: AI TOOLS | Impact of glass-boxing the Machine Learning pipeline on learning
projects.summary: Develop a custom web-based platform to run a study comparing three levels of transparency (glass box, gray box, black box) in a decision-tree machine learning task where users predict a dinosaur's diet from field notes. The project adapts an existing paper-based experiment to a digital environment to test whether exposing data preparation or model logic improves understanding of ML.

projects.title: AI TOOLS – Understanding Learning Through Pipeline Transparency
projects.summary: Student project on AI tools for education, examining how pipeline transparency helps learners understand learning.

projects.title: Testing a neutrality-detection tool
projects.summary: Final pre-deployment testing of a tool that localizes where ISPs throttle, block, or de-prioritize traffic. The work includes running experiments on various networks, analyzing results to evaluate accuracy and robustness, and suggesting improvements.

projects.title: Using math to infer network behavior
projects.summary: Infer network behavior, such as traffic de-prioritization, using only external observations of a flow. The student would help reconstruct the queuing delay process seen by a flow from its own irregular observations.

projects.title: [Performance/eBPF] Performance Modeling of eBPF Programs
projects.summary: Design a scalable and accurate performance model for eBPF programs that can quantify per-line performance, support performance debugging, and check new programs against functionally equivalent baselines.

projects.title: [Systems for ML] Improving the performance of ML workloads
projects.summary: Analyze and break down the software-stack overheads of ML inference and training, within a single machine and across machines. Based on this analysis, propose optimizations that improve the performance of these systems.

projects.title: Does Personalization in Medical Collaborative Learning Learn Site Shortcuts?
projects.summary: Investigates whether standard personalized federated learning methods learn site-specific shortcuts (spurious correlations) on medical data, with the goal of informing a personalization method that keeps useful site-specific features while avoiding shortcuts.

projects.title: Noise or Lies? Distinguishing privacy protection from fairwashing in black-box audits
projects.summary: Studies when an external auditor, who only sees black-box query answers, can distinguish an honest privacy-preserving platform (random, public noise) from a manipulative platform that performs fairwashing to hide discrimination.

projects.title: Privacy Vulnerability Transfer in Model Merging
projects.summary: Studies how privacy vulnerabilities, including membership inference and extraction risks, propagate into merged language models built with model merging and task arithmetic, and how merging coefficients, number of merged models and task similarity affect this transfer.

projects.title: Whose bubble is it? Harvesting idle capacity in data-parallel, expert-parallel LLM serving
